BK-KB-001: How should the platform count indirect sets (e.g., triceps contribution during pressing) in a way that is useful but not falsely precise?
What progression and fatigue markers are reliable and practical for novice users who do not know RIR/RPE?
Which sport-specific modules are required for each position/event and local competition calendar?
What clinical escalation pathways and South African emergency/healthcare resources should be displayed in-app?
How will the exercise library be independently reviewed for technique, accessibility, equipment safety and copyright-safe instructional media?
How should the generator account for sex, age, body size, disability and socioeconomic equipment access without stereotyping or overfitting?
BK-AI-002: Which South African clinical and emergency-care references should be integrated, and who owns updates?
What local language variants, slang and spelling patterns appear in Big Kat's actual user queries?
How will the system handle user-provided health data, consent, retention and privacy obligations?
Which clinical and sports-medicine experts will approve special-population content?
How will retrieval confidence be measured, and what threshold triggers a clarification rather than an answer?
How will the chatbot avoid over-personalising from unreliable or stale training logs?
Which questions should be answered by static FAQ, workout-plan generator, connected data or human professional referral?

BK-KB-001: Method: targeted evidence search on 10 November 2026 prioritising major consensus statements, public-health guidance, systematic reviews/meta-analyses and position stands. The most influential current adult resistance-training source identified was the 2026 ACSM overview of 137 systematic reviews (>30,000 participants), supplemented by WHO physical-activity guidance, a 2023 network meta-analysis, ISSN protein/creatine position stands, NSCA older-adult/youth guidance and ACOG pregnancy guidance. [S01–S10]

Limitations: this is a curated foundational synthesis, not a preregistered systematic review. The source set is strongest for general adult resistance training, public-health activity, protein/creatine basics and selected special populations. Evidence for specific sport programming, detailed injury rehabilitation, disability-specific adaptation, advanced peaking, hydration protocols and many individual exercises requires additional targeted reviews. The 2025 dose-response meta-regression [S11] is recent and informative but should be checked against full text, methods and subsequent replications before it drives automated dose limits.
BK-AI-002: The FAQ bank was developed by mapping common beginner, resistance-training, nutrition, cardio, recovery and safety intents to the selected evidence base. The content uses consensus and review literature where available, and coaching application where a single universally optimal answer does not exist. The FAQ set is a structured starter library, not a claim that every community question has been exhaustively sampled.

Community research limitation: this edition does not present Reddit or other forum anecdotes as scientific evidence. Community-derived language and questions should be collected in a separate discovery phase, tagged as user-reported experience, and never promoted to evidence without independent verification.

Versioning: review high-risk safety and special-population content at least annually and whenever major guidelines change. Review exercise science and supplement records when major position stands, systematic reviews or regulatory warnings appear.

records.source_scope_note: Important scope note: the 2026 ACSM resistance-training overview is a major recent synthesis of 137 systematic reviews and more than 30,000 participants, with searches current to October 2024. It concerns generally healthy adults; it does not replace clinical assessment or specialist programming for medical conditions, pregnancy complications, rehabilitation, or competitive sport-specific demands. [S01]
